Processes each encountered region for opaque-member checking, skipping bound regions and invoking the stored callback for all other regions.

Traverses only types that contain free regions and selectively visits the parts relevant for opaque lifetime constraints. Returns whether this `UseKind` represents a defining use, yielding true for `DefiningUse` and false for `OpaqueUse`.

Registers an inferred hidden type for an opaque definition and produces the obligations needed to justify it. Checks whether a named opaque type may be defined from the given local item by walking up the HIR parent chain from the item to see whether it reaches the opaque type’s defining scope.

Registers a hidden type for an opaque type when using the next trait solver. Constructs a `Coerce` helper with the given `FnCtxt`, obligation cause, and two-phase-borrow policy, initializing it in subtyping mode; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.

Performs the underlying type relation for coercion, using either LUB or supertype unification under a snapshot and, with the next solver, filtering out impossible obligations before succeeding; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.
Runs `unify` and, on success, converts the unified target type into adjustments and a final coercion result by calling `unify` and `success`.

Handles coercion when the source is an unresolved type variable: if both sides are unresolved it emits `Coerce` obligations toward a chosen target, otherwise it falls back to subtype/LUB unification by calling `unify_and`.

Implements coercions to borrowed references, including mutability checks, fallback when the source is not already a reference, and autoderef-plus-autoref reborrows that search for a matching referent. It explicitly calls `coerce_mutbls`, `unify_and`, `unify`, and `success`.

Shared helper for safe-function coercions that conditionally inserts a safe-to-unsafe fn-pointer conversion, otherwise performs normal unification, then leak-checks the snapshot before committing. It explicitly calls `unify_and`.

Handles coercion from a function pointer type, chiefly allowing safe-to-unsafe weakening through the shared helper. It explicitly calls `coerce_from_safe_fn`, `simple`, and uses `identity` for the non-adjusting path.

Handles coercion from a function item by normalizing the target, rejecting intrinsic and forbidden target-feature casts, reifying the item to a fn pointer when needed, and then delegating safe/unsafe function coercion; otherwise it falls back to plain unification. Coerces a non-capturing closure to a function pointer by constructing the unclosed fn-pointer signature and unifying it with a closure-fn-pointer adjustment; capturing closures or non-fn-pointer targets fall back to plain unification. Implements coercion to raw pointers from references or other raw pointers, checking mutability compatibility and choosing between reborrow-style raw-pointer formation, mut-to-const weakening, or no-op pointer unification. Predicate-style check for whether one type can coerce to another by probing a `Coerce` run and ensuring all produced obligations can be selected. It explicitly calls `Coerce::new` and `Coerce::coerce`.
Searches autoderef steps to find the first intermediate type that can unify with the target and returns that deref count. It explicitly calls `Coerce::new` and `Coerce::unify`.
Diagnostic helper that autodereferences once and returns the dereferenced type only if the original type may implement `DerefMut`; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.

Computes a coercion-aware least upper bound across expressions, first trying ordinary LUB, then special-casing distinct function items and non-capturing closures by reifying them to compatible fn pointers and applying the resulting adjustments to prior coercion sites. It explicitly calls `Coerce::new` and `FnCtxt::coerce`.
Constructs a `CoerceMany` accumulator with dynamic storage for coercion sites. It explicitly calls `CoerceMany::make`.
Constructs a `CoerceMany` accumulator using a pre-supplied slice of coercion sites. It explicitly calls `CoerceMany::make`.
Internal constructor that initializes the expected type, optional merged type, expression storage, and push count for `CoerceMany`; it does not call any other method from the listed methods.

Adds one expression to the multi-expression coercion process by delegating to the internal coercion driver. It explicitly calls `coerce_inner`.
Forces the next coerced value to have type `()`, delegating all work to `coerce_inner` with the unit type and no expression node.

Emits a diagnostic note for a loop expression whose body may never execute, explaining that expected return values from collected `ret_exprs` could be unreachable. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Builds a detailed diagnostic for return-position coercion failures. Determines whether the enclosing function's return type is definitely not `Sized`. It calls `body_fn_sig` to get the function signature and `predicate_may_hold` on a constructed `Sized` obligation over `sig.output()`.
Finishes coercion accumulation by returning the computed final type if one exists, or `!` when no non-never inputs were successfully pushed.
Trait requirement that returns the HIR expression to use as the coercion site; it does not call other listed methods.
Returns the expression itself as the coercion site; it does not call other listed methods.
Forwards coercion-site lookup through a shared reference by calling `as_coercion_site` on the underlying `T`.

Augments a diagnostic for return-type coercion failures involving `impl Trait` by labeling the return type and offending expression, resolving the expected type for display, and adding notes about `impl Trait` requirements and trait objects. This method does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Checks a `break` expression by consulting the enclosing breakable context, type-checking any break value with `check_expr_with_hint`, and coercing it into the loop’s break accumulator while producing targeted diagnostics for illegal or mismatched break values.

Checks a `return` expression by calling `emit_return_outside_of_fn_body` when outside a function body, otherwise either type-checking the returned value with `check_return_expr` or forcing unit into the return coercion; when outside a function but a value is present, it still calls `check_expr` on that value for error recovery.

Checks a return value inside a function by reading the expected return type from the return coercion, calling `check_expr_with_hint` on the returned expression, coercing it into the function return via the return coercion, and then calling `select_obligations_where_possible` to reroute opaque-type errors through `point_at_return_for_opaque_ty_error` when needed.
Rewrites fulfillment errors caused by `OpaqueReturnType(None)` so they point at the specific return expression span and type instead of a broader enclosing block span.

Validates that an assignment left-hand side is a syntactic place expression, and if not, produces a tailored diagnostic that may call `comes_from_while_condition` and `check_for_missing_semi` before applying caller-supplied error adjustments.
Walks parent HIR nodes to determine whether an expression originated from a `while` condition and, if so, invokes the provided callback on that condition expression.

Checks an `if`/`if-else` by calling `check_expr_has_type_or_error` on the condition, `warn_if_unreachable` for the then-branch, `check_expr_with_expectation` on each branch, and then coercing branch types together with branch-specific diagnostics and divergence tracking.

Checks assignment expressions by computing the expected unit-like result, issuing `=` vs `==` diagnostics when boolean context suggests it, type-checking operands via `check_expr`, `check_expr_with_needs`, and `check_expr_with_hint`, enforcing RHS-to-LHS coercion with `demand_coerce_diag`, and validating assignability with `check_lhs_assignable`.
Checks a `let` expression by calling `warn_if_unreachable` on its initializer and `check_decl` with statement-style rules, then returns `bool` unless recovery marked the expression as erroneous.

Checks loop expressions by creating an optional break-value coercion target from the expectation, running the body through `with_breakable_ctxt` and `check_block_no_value`, updating divergence based on whether breaks occur, and completing the accumulated break coercion when present.

Checks a method call by calling `check_expr` on the receiver, resolving its type, looking up the method with `lookup_method`, recording successful resolution with `write_method_call_and_enforce_effects` or diagnosing failure with `report_method_error`, and then calling `check_method_argument_types`.

Checks a cast by lowering the target type, calling `check_expr_with_expectation` on the source with `ExpectCastableToType`, resolving both sides, and either returning an immediate error or deferring the detailed validation through `cast::CastCheck::new`.

Checks array literals by choosing an element coercion target from the expectation or a fresh type variable, calling `check_expr_with_hint` for each element, coercing them through a `CoerceMany`, then calling `suggest_array_len` and returning the resulting array type.

Looks up the enclosing typed array context for an expression and, when it finds an inferred array-length placeholder, emits a diagnostic suggesting the concrete `array_len`. It does not call other listed methods.

Type-checks a const block in a fresh `FnCtxt`: it gathers locals, checks the body against the given expectation, enforces that the resulting type is sized, records the block type, and returns it. This method calls the listed method `check_expr_with_expectation`.

Type-checks an array repeat expression `[element; count]` by lowering/evaluating the length, optionally suggesting an explicit array length, deriving the element type from the expected array/slice type when possible, checking the element, enforcing repeat-copy requirements, building the array type, and registering a well-formedness obligation. Determines whether a repeat-expression element must satisfy `Copy`, exempting true constants and const blocks, classifying const-call/const-constructor cases for diagnostics, and requiring the `Copy` lang-item obligation only when the evaluated repeat count may exceed 1. Type-checks a tuple expression by extracting expected field types from an expected tuple when available, coercing matching elements to those types, otherwise checking elements with no expectation, assembling the tuple type, propagating error types, and requiring the tuple initializer to be sized. Type-checks a struct literal by resolving the struct path, recovering by checking subexpressions on path-resolution failure, rejecting external non-exhaustive struct construction, checking all provided/base fields, and requiring the resulting ADT type to be sized. Checks the fields of a struct literal against the chosen variant: it reconciles expectation-derived hints with the ADT type, tracks remaining and duplicate fields, resolves each supplied field, records field indices, validates stability and field types, reports unknown fields, checks field expressions with hints/coercions, registers well-formedness obligations, and emits diagnostics for missing fields or FRU-related mistakes. Performs error-recovery checking for struct literal contents by still type-checking every explicit field expression and the optional base expression. This method calls the listed method `check_expr`.

Builds and emits the missing-fields diagnostic for a struct literal, formatting a readable list of omitted fields and, when there is at least one written field, delegating to a FRU typo suggestion path before emission. This method calls the listed method `suggest_fru_from_range_and_emit`.

Detects when the last struct field expression is a half-open `Range` literal that likely should be functional record update syntax (`..expr`) instead of a field value, suppresses any previously stashed range type-mismatch diagnostic, extracts a short printable snippet for the range end, computes the span covering the mistaken `..` region, and attaches a `TypeMismatchFruTypo` subdiagnostic to the provided error. This method does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Reports that a struct literal cannot be constructed because of private fields, distinguishing explicitly used versus merely remaining private fields, labeling or noting them, and searching inherent impl items for constructor-like associated functions whose signatures match the ADT so it can suggest alternatives. It does not call other listed methods.

Emits the diagnostic for using an unknown field in a struct/variant literal, tailoring the message for enum variants vs other ADTs, suggesting tuple-style constructor syntax for tuple variants, and offering likely field-name corrections based on available visible fields. This method calls the listed methods `available_field_names` and `name_series_display`.
Builds a list of accessible, stable field names for a variant while skipping already-used names, then returns the closest match to the requested field by calling `find_best_match_for_name`.

Collects suggestable field names from a variant, excluding fields already present in `skip_fields` and filtering through field-suggestability checks. This method calls the listed method `is_field_suggestable`.
Formats a bounded, human-readable comma-separated series of field names, appending an `... and N others` suffix when the list is longer than the display limit. It does not call other listed methods.

When the base type is an `impl Future`, checks whether the requested field exists on the future's `Output` type and, if so, suggests inserting `.await`; otherwise it just labels the field as unknown. It does not call other listed methods.

Builds and emits the main diagnostic for accessing a nonexistent field, specializing suggestions for arrays, raw pointers, type parameters, and opaque futures, then trying a method-call suggestion if calling the base expression would yield a type with the requested field, and adding the Rust-2018 `.await` note when relevant. Emits the private-field-access diagnostic and, when appropriate, suggests calling an accessible method with the same name instead of reading the field. This method calls the listed method `private_field_err`.

Reports the error for treating a method as a field value, then suggests either removing wrapping parentheses for an accidental call pattern, adding call parentheses, or dereferencing first for raw-pointer-to-ADT cases where the field exists after dereference. It does not call other listed methods.

Augments a diagnostic for field access on a type parameter by locating the non-synthetic type parameter declaration in the current body and labeling where that parameter was introduced. It does not call other listed methods.

Produces diagnostics for an unknown field on a struct-like ADT: it first calls `suggest_field_name` to offer a similar field name, and if none is found, it labels the access and lists available fields using `available_field_names` and `name_series_display`.

For mistaken tuple-style field syntax on arrays, labels the field as unknown and, when the field parses as an integer and the array length is evaluable, suggests rewriting `.n` as `[n]` with an applicability tuned by bounds confidence. It does not call other listed methods.
For raw-pointer field access, labels the field as unknown and suggests wrapping the base expression in an explicit dereference before accessing the field. It does not call other listed methods.

Constructs the base `no field` diagnostic and enriches it with suggestions for nested-field access paths, misspelled field names, and visible candidate field listings; it also unwraps `Option`/`Result`-like outer types when searching for nested matches. Constructs the base diagnostic for accessing a private field, naming the enclosing item and labeling the offending field span. It does not call other listed methods.

Autodereferences a base type and gathers visible, suggestable fields from non-enum ADTs, skipping wrappers whose fields are all private and capping the number of searched fields for compile-time cost. This method calls the listed method `is_field_suggestable`.

Recursively searches through visible nested ADT fields up to depth three for a field satisfying the provided predicate, extending and returning the field path on success. Scans fulfillment errors for `SliceIndex` trait obligations and, when found, rewrites their cause span to the provided span so indexing-related diagnostics point at the expression location.

Checks a `yield` expression against the current coroutine context.
